senses.gloss: m. (יָרַד) meeting-place, market, annual fair generally dedicated to a deity.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 11b:8">Ab. Zar. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>י׳ שבעין בכי י׳ שבעכו</he>, (Ms. M. <cite ref="J00604"><he>ירוד</he></cite>, <he>ירור</he>) a market-place (with the idol) at Baalbek, at Acco (v. <cite ref="N00210"><he>נִדְבָּכָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 13a:4">Ib. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>הנושא ונותן בי׳ של גוים</he> (Ms. M. ed. <he>בשוק של עכ״ום</he>) one who deals at a fair of gentiles.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 13a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>הולכין לי׳ של עכ״ום וכ׳</he> one may go to an idolatrous fair and buy there &c.; Y. ib. I, 39ᵇ; ᶜ bot. (only) <he>הולכין ליריד</he>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 47:10">Gen. R. s. 47</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>יְרִידִים</he>, <he>יְרִידִין</he>. Y. l. c. 39ᵈ top <he>ג׳ י׳ הן וכ׳</he> there are three (Palestinean) fairs, that of Gaza &c.; Gen. R. l. c.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 67:7">Gen. R. s. 67</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 115:22">Yalk. Gen. 115</cite> [read:] <he>את לך י׳ והוא יש לו שווקים</he> thou (Esau-Rome) hast fairs, and he (Israel) has markets (i.e. you compete in commerce); a. e.
